questions.question:
In the year 1916, which of the following month had 5 Wednesdays?

I. June II. December
questions.solution:
__**Concept:**__

The number of times a particular day occurs in a month depends on the total **number of days** in that month and the **day of the week** it starts on:

__
 
• A month with **30 days** will have 5 of a specific day if the month starts on that day or the day before it (i.e., the day must fall on the **1st** or **2nd** of the month).
 
• A month with **31 days** will have 5 of a specific day if the month starts on that day or up to two days before it (i.e., the day must fall on the **1st**, **2nd**, or **3rd** of the month).

**Calculation:**__

The year **1916** is divisible by 4, making it a **leap year**. Therefore, **February** has 29 days.

First, we determine the day of the week for **January 1, 1916**. Using the calendar calculation, January 1, 1916, was a **Saturday**.

**I. June 1916**

**June** always has **30 days**.

Total days from January 1 to **June 1** = 31 (Jan) + 29 (Feb) + 31 (Mar) + 30 (Apr) + 31 (May) = 152 days.

Odd days = 152 ÷ 7 = 21 weeks and **5 odd days**.

Day on **June 1** = Saturday + 5 days = **Thursday**.

Since June starts on a **Thursday**, the **Wednesdays** fall on the 7th, 14th, 21st, and 28th. There are only **4 Wednesdays** in June 1916.

**II. December 1916**

**December** always has **31 days**.

Total days from June 1 to **December 1** = 30 (Jun) + 31 (Jul) + 31 (Aug) + 30 (Sep) + 31 (Oct) + 30 (Nov) = 183 days.

Odd days = 183 ÷ 7 = 26 weeks and **1 odd day**.

Day on **December 1** = Thursday + 1 day = **Friday**.

Since December starts on a **Friday**, the **Wednesdays** fall on the 6th, 13th, 20th, and 27th. There are only **4 Wednesdays** in December 1916.

Therefore, neither June nor December had 5 Wednesdays in the year **1916**.

Therefore, the correct option is **4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

We can use the day of the week formula: Day = (Date + Month Code + Year Code + Century Code + Leap Year Adjustment) mod 7.

For the year **1916**: Year = 16, Leap Year count = 16 ÷ 4 = 4. Century Code (1900s) = 0.

For **June 1** (Month Code = 4): (1 + 4 + 16 + 4 + 0) mod 7 = 25 mod 7 = 4 (**Thursday**).

For **December 1** (Month Code = 5): (1 + 5 + 16 + 4 + 0) mod 7 = 26 mod 7 = 5 (**Friday**).

A **30-day month** (June) needs to start on Tuesday or Wednesday to have 5 Wednesdays. A **31-day month** (December) needs to start on Monday, Tuesday, or Wednesday to have 5 Wednesdays.

Since June started on **Thursday** and December started on **Friday**, neither month had **5 Wednesdays**.

Hence, the correct answer is **Neither I nor II**.

questions.question: At what time (approximately) (in AM) between 10 AM and 11 AM will the angle between the hour and the minute hand of a clock be 15 degrees?
questions.solution:
__**Concept:**__

**Hour hand** covers 3600 in 12 hours.

Angular distance covered in 1 hour = 360/12 = 300

Angular distance covered by the **hour hand** in 1 minute = 30/60 = 0.50

**Minute hand** covers 3600 in 60 minutes.

Angular distance covered in 1 minute = 360/60 = 60

**__Calculation:__**

The given time is between **10 AM** and **11 AM**. Let the time be **10:M**.

At **10:00 AM**, the hour hand is at 10 × 300 = 3000 and the minute hand is at 00.

In **M** minutes:

Position of the **hour hand** = 3000 + 0.5 × M

Position of the **minute hand** = 6 × M

Angle between hands = |(300 + 0.5M) − 6M| = |300 − 5.5M|

Given the angle is **15 degrees**:

**Case 1:**

300 − 5.5M = 15 ⇒ 5.5M = 285

M = 285 / 5.5 ≈ 51.81 minutes

**Case 2:**

300 − 5.5M = −15 ⇒ 5.5M = 315

M = 315 / 5.5 ≈ 57.27 minutes

The approximate time from **Case 1** is **10:52 AM** (since 51.81 ≈ 52).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

The angle between the **hour hand** and **minute hand** = |60H - 11M| over 2

Here, H = 10 and Angle = 15.

15 = |60 times 10 - 11 times M| over 2

30 = |600 − 11M|

600 − 11M = 30 ⇒ 11M = 570 ⇒ M = 51.818...

600 − 11M = −30 ⇒ 11M = 630 ⇒ M = 57.272...

The closest value to the options is 51.82, which is approximately 52 minutes.

Hence, the correct answer is **10:52**

questions.question: At what time (approximately) (in PM) between 3 PM and 4 PM will the angle between the hour and the minute hand of a clock be 110 degrees?
questions.solution:
__**Concept:**__

The angle between the **hour hand** and the **minute hand** of a clock can be calculated using the following relationship:

Angle (θ) = |30H − 5.5M|

Where:

__
 
• **H** is the hour (in this case, **3**).
 
• **M** is the minutes past the hour.

Alternatively, we can look at the relative speeds:

Speed of the **minute hand** = 6° per minute

Speed of the **hour hand** = 0.5° per minute

The relative speed between the two hands is 5.5° per minute.

**Calculation:__**

We are looking for the time between **3 PM** and **4 PM** when the angle is **110 degrees**.

Given **H = 3** and **θ = 110°**.

Case 1: The minute hand is behind the hour hand (not possible for 110° starting from 3 PM, as 3:00 is only 90°).

Case 2: The minute hand is ahead of the hour hand.

110 = 5.5M − 30(3)

110 = 5.5M − 90

110 + 90 = 5.5M

200 = 5.5M

M = 200 ÷ 5.5

M = 400 ÷ 11

M = 36.3636...

Rounding to the nearest minute, we get **M ≈ 36**.

Therefore, the time is approximately **3:36 PM**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

At **3:00 PM**, the angle between the hands is 90°.

To reach an angle of **110°**, the minute hand must first cover the 90° to overlap the hour hand and then move 110° ahead of it.

Total relative distance to be covered = 90° + 110° = 200°

Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

Time = 200 ÷ 5.5

Time = 36.36 minutes

The approximate time is **3:36 PM**.

Hence, the correct answer is **3:36**.

questions.question: The ratio of present ages of M and S is 2 : 5. M is 9 years younger than S. What will be the ratio of M's age to S's age after 12 years?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Present age ratio of M and S = **2 : 5**

M is **9 years younger** than S.

**Calculation:**

Let the present ages of M and S be **2x** and **5x**.

Difference = 5x − 2x = 9

3x = 9

x = 3

Present ages:

 
• M = 2 × 3 = **6 years**
 
• S = 5 × 3 = **15 years**

**After 12 years:**

M = 6 + 12 = **18 years**

S = 15 + 12 = **27 years**

**Required ratio:**

18 : 27 = 2 : 3

Hence, the correct answer is** "Option 1".**

questions.question: In whose court is the celebrated Sanskrit poet Kalidasa believed to have flourished?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chandragupta II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kalidasa**, widely regarded as the greatest poet and dramatist in the **Sanskrit** language, is historically associated with the court of **Chandragupta II**.
 
• He was celebrated as one of the **Navaratnas** (Nine Gems), a group of nine distinguished scholars and artists who graced the royal court of the **Gupta Empire**.
 
• **Chandragupta II**, who assumed the prestigious title of **Vikramaditya**, ruled from approximately **380 CE to 415 CE**, marking the peak of the **Gupta Golden Age**.
 
• The poet's works, including the world-renowned drama **Abhijnanashakuntalam** and epic poems like **Meghaduta** and **Kumarasambhava**, reflect the cultural sophistication and religious harmony of the **Gupta era**.
 
• While the primary capital was **Pataliputra**, **Chandragupta II** maintained a secondary capital at **Ujjain**, which became a significant center for literary and scientific advancements where **Kalidasa** flourished.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Samudragupta**:

 
 
• Often referred to as the **Napoleon of India** by historian **V.A. Smith** due to his extensive military conquests.
 
• He was a versatile genius and a poet himself, earning the title **Kaviraja** (King of Poets).
 
 
 
• **Kumaragupta**:
 
 
• The son and successor of **Chandragupta II**, his reign saw the establishment of the famous **Nalanda University**.
 
• He was a worshiper of **Lord Kartikeya** and performed the **Ashvamedha** sacrifice to assert his imperial authority.
 
 
 
• **Skandagupta**:
 
 
• Recognized as the last great **Gupta Emperor**, he is famous for successfully defending the empire against the **Hunas** (Huns).
 
• His achievements are inscribed on the **Bhitari Pillar** and the **Junagarh Rock**.

questions.question:
Which pressure belt is being talked about in the information given below?

"This pressure belt is found between 30°N to 35°N latitude and this is also known as horse latitude."
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sub-tropical high pressure belt**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Sub-tropical high pressure belt** is located in both hemispheres between approximately **30°N to 35°N** and **30°S to 35°S** latitudes.
 
• This belt is also famously known as the **Horse Latitudes** due to the calm winds and high pressure that historically stalled sailing ships.
 
• The formation of this belt is primarily due to the **subsidence** of air; air that rises at the **Equator** (Hadley Cell) cools as it moves poleward and descends at these latitudes, creating **high-pressure** conditions at the surface.
 
• Characterized by **anticyclonic** conditions, this region experiences light winds, clear skies, and low humidity, which is why most of the world's **hot deserts** (like the Sahara and Arabian deserts) are located along these latitudes.
 
• The term **Horse Latitudes** originated because sailors, when becalmed for long periods, had to throw **horses** overboard to conserve drinking water for the crew.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Equatorial Low Pressure Belt**:

 
 
• Located between **5°N and 5°S** latitudes.
 
• Known as the **Doldrums**, it is a zone of convergence for trade winds and intense solar heating.
 
 
 
• **Sub-polar Low Pressure Belt**:
 
 
• Situated between **60° and 65°** latitudes in both hemispheres.
 
• Formed by the convergence of warm **Westerlies** and cold **Polar Easterlies**, leading to the development of **temperate cyclones**.
 
 
 
• **Polar High Pressure Belt**:
 
 
• Located around the **North and South Poles** (80°−90°).
 
• Caused by extremely low temperatures which make the air dense, leading to constant **high pressure** and cold, dry conditions.

questions.question: What is the change of state from liquid to gas at atmospheric pressure known as?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vaporisation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vaporisation** refers to the physical transition of a substance from the **liquid phase** to the **gaseous phase**.
 
• At **atmospheric pressure**, this change occurs when molecules in the liquid gain sufficient **thermal energy** to overcome the **intermolecular attractive forces** (such as hydrogen bonding or Van der Waals forces) that hold them in a condensed state.
 
• This process encompasses two distinct phenomena: **evaporation**, which is a surface-level transition occurring at any temperature, and **boiling**, which occurs throughout the bulk of the liquid at a specific **boiling point**.
 
• When a liquid reaches its boiling point at **1 atmospheric pressure** (101.325 kPa), the **vapour pressure** of the liquid becomes equal to the external atmospheric pressure.
 
• The transition requires an input of energy known as the **Latent Heat of Vaporisation**, which increases the potential energy of the particles without raising the temperature during the phase change.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Solidification and Freezing:**

 
 
• **Solidification** (often called **freezing**) is the phase change from **liquid to solid**.
 
• This process occurs when **kinetic energy** is removed, allowing particles to settle into a fixed, ordered **crystalline lattice** or an amorphous structure.
 
 
 
• **Deposition:**
 
 
• **Deposition** is a **thermodynamic process** where a substance transforms directly from a **gas to a solid**, bypassing the liquid state entirely.
 
• A common natural example is the formation of **sub-freezing hoar frost** on ground surfaces or the transformation of water vapour into **snow** in clouds.

questions.question: When was the gender budgeting introduced in India?

__
 
• **Gender Budgeting** was formally introduced in India during the **Union Budget 2005-2006** under the leadership of the then Finance Minister **P. Chidambaram**.
 
• It is not a separate budget for women but a **fiscal strategy** and analytical tool used to examine the government budget through a **gender lens** to ensure equitable distribution of resources.
 
• The introduction featured the first **Gender Budget Statement**, originally known as **Statement 20** (now **Statement 13**), which disclosed the allocations specifically targeting women.
 
• The process categorizes schemes into two parts: **Part A**, which includes schemes with **100% allocation** for women, and **Part B**, which includes schemes where at least **30% of the allocation** is earmarked for women.
 
• India became one of the pioneering developing nations to institutionalize **Gender Responsive Budgeting (GRB)** to address gender gaps in education, health, and economic opportunities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Institutional Mechanisms**:

 
 
• The **Ministry of Women and Child Development (MWCD)** is the nodal agency for the implementation and monitoring of gender budgeting across various sectors.
 
• Following the **2005-2006** mandate, **Gender Budget Cells (GBCs)** were established within various central ministries and departments to facilitate gender-sensitive planning and evaluation.
 
• The **National Institute of Public Finance and Policy (NIPFP)** provided the initial analytical framework that helped the government transition from a general budget to a gender-sensitive one.
 
 
 
• **Evolution and Background**:
 
 
• The groundwork was laid during the **Ninth Five-Year Plan (1997-2002)**, which introduced the **Women's Component Plan (WCP)** to ensure that 30% of funds from all ministries were directed toward women.
 
• In **2004**, an **Expert Group** was constituted to recommend a classification system for government expenditure to track pro-women allocations effectively.
 
• While it started with only **10 ministries** in its inaugural year, the scope of the **Gender Budget Statement** has expanded significantly, now covering over **30 ministries** and departments.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **2005-2006**

• **Characteristics and Global Significance:**

 
 
• **Definition:** A mineral is classified as 'critical' when it is essential for **economic growth** and **national security**, while its supply chain is prone to disruption due to geological scarcity or geopolitical factors.
 
• **Rare Earth Elements (REEs):** A group of 17 minerals used in **permanent magnets** for **wind turbines** and **EV motors**, currently dominated by **China** in terms of mining and processing.
 
• **Indian Context:** The **Ministry of Mines** released a list of **30 critical minerals** in 2023, including **Beryllium**, **Germanium**, and **Titanium**, to bolster the **Atmanirbhar Bharat** initiative and secure **domestic manufacturing**.
 
• **International Alliances:** India has joined the **Mineral Security Partnership (MSP)**, a US-led initiative aimed at accelerating the development of diverse and sustainable critical energy minerals supply chains globally.
 
• **Supply Chain Vulnerability:** Unlike oil, which is traded on a liquid global market, critical minerals often have highly concentrated production sites, leading to **strategic dependencies** and the need for **bilateral trade agreements**.

questions.question:

questions.solution:

__

It is characterized by simultaneous arm movements on a horizontal plane and a **frog-like kick** (whip kick). It is widely regarded as the oldest and slowest of the four competitive strokes. ***Hence, statement I is correct.***
 
• The **Backstroke** (or back crawl) is unique because it is the only competitive stroke performed with the swimmer lying on their **back**. It involves alternating arm movements and a **flutter kick**. A key advantage of this stroke is that it allows for easy breathing, though swimmers cannot see where they are going. ***Hence, statement II is correct.***
 
• Both **Breaststroke** and **Backstroke** are officially recognized by **World Aquatics** (formerly FINA) as standard competitive disciplines in international events like the **Olympic Games** and **World Championships**.

• **Freestyle (Front Crawl)**:

 
 
• It is the **fastest** and most efficient swimming stroke.
 
• Characterized by an alternating overhand arm motion and a continuous **flutter kick**.
 
• Swimmers breathe by rotating their heads to the side.
 
 
 
• **Butterfly Stroke**:
 
 
• Regarded as the most **physically demanding** and technically difficult stroke.
 
• Features a simultaneous overhead arm recovery and a **dolphin kick** where the legs move together.
 
• It was developed as a variation of the breaststroke before becoming its own category in **1952**.
 
 
 
• **Individual Medley (IM)**:
 
 
• A single swimmer performs all four strokes in a specific order: **Butterfly**, **Backstroke**, **Breaststroke**, and **Freestyle**.

questions.question: What is the smallest 4-digit number that is divisible by 36?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

A number divisible by **36** must be divisible by both **4** and **9** (**36 = 4 × 9**).

Check the **divisibility rule of 9** (sum of digits) for the options:

(1) 1036: 1+0+3+6 = 10 | (2) **1008**: 1+0+0+8 = **9** | (3) 1016: 1+0+1+6 = 8 | (4) 1028: 1+0+2+8 = 11.

Only **1008** is divisible by **9** and its last two digits (**08**) are divisible by **4**.

**∴ The correct answer is 1008.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Smallest **4-digit number** = **1000**

Divisor = **36**

**Method:**

Divide the smallest **4-digit number** by **36** to find the **remainder**, then adjust to find the next multiple.

**Calculations:**

⇒ **1000 ÷ 36**

⇒ **36 × 27 = 972**

⇒ **Remainder = 1000 − 972 = 28**

⇒ To find the next multiple, add (**Divisor − Remainder**) to the number.

⇒ **Adjustment = 36 − 28 = 8**

⇒ **Smallest 4-digit multiple = 1000 + 8 = 1008**

**∴ The correct answer is 1008.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility Rule of 9

A number is divisible by **9** if the **sum of its digits** is a multiple of **9**.

Divisibility Rule of 4

A number is divisible by **4** if its **last two digits** are divisible by **4** or are both zero.

Smallest n-digit Multiple

Smallest multiple = **Smallest n-digit number + (Divisor − Remainder)**, where the remainder comes from dividing the smallest n-digit number by the divisor.

questions.question: What is the largest 2 digit number which is exactly divisible by both 8 and 7?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Find the **LCM** of 8 and 7 to get the smallest number divisible by both.

**LCM(8, 7)** = 8 × 7 = **56** (since they are co-prime).

The next multiple is 56 × 2 = **112**, which is a 3-digit number.

Thus, the **largest 2-digit number** divisible by both is 56.

**∴ The correct answer is 56.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Divisors = **8** and **7**

Target = **Largest 2-digit number** exactly divisible by both.

**Formula Used:**

A number divisible by multiple numbers is also divisible by their **Least Common Multiple (LCM)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1c4f6a693ccb6aa7096bb8568dd21fa4934519f4b81a3ecf1fddcb502bf52c72.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Step 1: Calculate the **LCM** of 8 and 7.

⇒ Prime factorization of 8 = 2 × 2 × 2

⇒ Prime factorization of 7 = 7

⇒ **LCM(8, 7)** = 2³ × 7 = 56

⇒ Step 2: List the multiples of 56 to find the **largest 2-digit** one.

⇒ 56 × 1 = **56**

⇒ 56 × 2 = **112**

⇒ Since 112 is a **3-digit number** and the maximum 2-digit number is 99, 112 is excluded.

⇒ The largest 2-digit multiple is therefore 56.

**∴ The correct answer is 56.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Least Common Multiple (LCM)

The smallest positive integer that is a multiple of two or more numbers. For **co-prime** numbers (numbers with HCF = 1), the LCM is always the **product** of the numbers.

Co-prime Numbers Property

If **a** and **b** are co-prime, then any number divisible by both **a** and **b** must also be divisible by their product (**a × b**).

Divisibility Rule of 8 and 7

A number is divisible by 8 if its last three digits are divisible by 8. For 7, subtract twice the last digit from the remaining number; if the result is divisible by 7, the original number is too.

questions.question: A is (1/5) of B. A is how much percent less than B?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **A : B = 1 : 5**

Value of **B** is 5 units and **A** is 1 unit.

Difference = 5 − 1 = **4 units**.

Percentage less = (Difference ÷ Value of B) × 100 = (4 ÷ 5) × 100 = **80%**.

**∴ The correct answer is 80 percent.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**A** = (1/5) × **B**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ab3a73843e31fe5a5b70cbb99cff93a3637d059363e34e396246335a9791938e.png] 

**Calculation:**

⇒ **A / B = 1 / 5**

⇒ Let **B** = 5x and **A** = 1x

⇒ **Difference** = B − A = 5x − 1x = 4x

⇒ **Percentage less** = (Difference ÷ B) × 100

⇒ Percentage less = (4x ÷ 5x) × 100

⇒ Percentage less = (4 ÷ 5) × 100 = **80%**

**∴ The correct answer is 80 percent.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Decrease Formula

Percentage Less = [(Reference Value − Target Value) ÷ Reference Value] × 100.

Fraction to Percentage Conversion

To convert any fraction x/y into percentage, multiply the fraction by 100 (e.g., 1/5 × 100 = 20%).

Complementary Percentages

If A is 20% of B, then A is (100% − 20%) = 80% less than B.

questions.question: A person sells an article at the loss of 40 percent. Cost price and selling price both are decreased by 50 percent. What will be the new loss percentage?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If both the **Cost Price (CP)** and **Selling Price (SP)** are multiplied or divided by the same factor (or decreased/increased by the same percentage), the **ratio** between them remains unchanged.

Since both CP and SP are decreased by **50%**, they are both halved, keeping the ratio **CP : SP** constant.

Original ratio ⇒ CP : SP = 100 : 60 (for a 40% loss).

New ratio ⇒ 50 : 30 = 100 : 60.

Because the ratio is unchanged, the **loss percentage** remains **40%**.

**∴ The correct answer is 40 percent.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Initial Loss % = 40%, Reduction in CP and SP = 50%.

**Formula Used:** Loss % = [(CP − SP) ÷ CP] × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f70c014c6d5a6c9c1260d30a7b56d50a4e6575be8a9659d96a3012114beb0305.png] 

⇒ Let the initial **Cost Price (CP₁)** = 100.

⇒ Initial **Selling Price (SP₁)** = CP₁ − 40% of CP₁ = 100 − 40 = 60.

⇒ New **Cost Price (CP₂)** = 100 − 50% of 100 = 50.

⇒ New **Selling Price (SP₂)** = 60 − 50% of 60 = 30.

⇒ New **Loss Amount** = CP₂ − SP₂ = 50 − 30 = 20.

⇒ New **Loss Percentage** = (New Loss ÷ CP₂) × 100

⇒ New **Loss Percentage** = (20 ÷ 50) × 100 = 40%.

**∴ The correct answer is 40 percent.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss % Invariance

The profit or loss percentage remains unchanged if both the Cost Price and Selling Price are multiplied or divided by the same non-zero constant (constant ratio).

Loss Percentage Formula

Loss % is calculated as (Loss ÷ CP) × 100. It measures the loss relative to the initial investment (CP).

Successive Changes in CP and SP

If CP changes by x% and SP changes by y%, the new profit/loss % must be calculated using the new values: New % = [(SP × (1+y/100) − CP × (1+x/100)) ÷ (CP × (1+x/100))] × 100.

questions.question: P got 20 percent less marks than Q. R got 50 percent less marks than Q. If sum of P, R and Q marks is 2300, then what is the difference between the marks of Q and R?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of marks **P : Q : R** = 80 : 100 : 50 = **8 : 10 : 5**

Total sum of ratio units = 8 + 10 + 5 = **23 units**

Given 23 units = **2300** → 1 unit = **100**

Difference between **Q** and **R** = 10 − 5 = **5 units**

Required difference = 5 × 100 = **500**

**∴ The correct answer is 500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cc816170891d7e90e1e7346abede4252995e125a21451946ed57df163d069ebb.png] 

**Given:**

Marks of **P** = **Q** − 20% of **Q** = 0.8**Q**

Marks of **R** = **Q** − 50% of **Q** = 0.5**Q**

Sum of marks (**P + Q + R**) = **2300**

**Calculations:**

⇒ 0.8**Q** + 1.0**Q** + 0.5**Q** = 2300

⇒ 2.3**Q** = 2300

⇒ **Q** = 2300 ÷ 2.3 = **1000**

⇒ **R** = 0.5 × 1000 = **500**

⇒ Difference = **Q − R** = 1000 − 500 = **500**

**∴ The correct answer is 500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage to Ratio Conversion

Comparing values by converting percentages to units simplifies calculations significantly in competitive exams.

Percentage Change Formula

Final Value = Initial Value × (100 ± x)/100, where x is the percentage increase or decrease.

Difference between Values

The difference between two quantities can be found directly from their ratio parts without calculating individual values first: Difference = (Diff in parts ÷ Sum of parts) × Total Sum.

questions.question: 25 men can complete a work in 60 days. 15 men will complete 50 percent of the same work in how many days?

Total work capacity = **25 men** × **60 days** = 1500 units.

Target work (**50% work**) = 1500 ÷ 2 = 750 units.

Days required for **15 men** = 750 ÷ 15 = **50 days**.

**∴ The correct answer is 50 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Initial days (D₁) = **60 days**

Target men (M₂) = **15 men**

Work ratio = W₁ is 1, W₂ is 0.5 (**50 percent**)

**Formula Used:**

(M₁ × D₁) ÷ W₁ = (M₂ × D₂) ÷ W₂

**Calculations:**

⇒ (25 × 60) ÷ 1 = (15 × D₂) ÷ 0.5

⇒ 1500 = 30 × D₂

⇒ D₂ = 1500 ÷ 30

Chain Rule Formula

Used to solve problems with multiple variables: (M₁×D₁×H₁)/W₁ = (M₂×D₂×H₂)/W₂, where M is men, D is days, H is hours, and W is work.

Efficiency is **inversely proportional** to the time taken to complete the work (Efficiency ∝ 1/Time).

questions.question: R, M and T work for 4 days, 6 days and 8 days respectively. They get a total amount of Rs. 540 for their work. Ratio of one day work of R, M and T is 1 : 2 : 3 respectively. How much money (in Rs.) does M get?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of total work done (and thus **wages**) is Efficiency × Days.

Ratio of shares (R : M : T) = (1 × 4) : (2 × 6) : (3 × 8) = 4 : 12 : 24 = 1 : 3 : 6.

Total units = 1 + 3 + 6 = 10 units → ₹540.

1 unit = ₹54 ∴ M's share = 3 units = 3 × ₹54 = ₹162.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹162.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time worked by **R** = 4 days, **M** = 6 days, **T** = 8 days.

One day work (Efficiency) ratio **R : M : T** = 1 : 2 : 3.

Total amount distributed = **₹540**.

**Formula Used:**

Individual Wage = (Efficiency × Number of Days worked)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7fd120777b781918a9b720aea17a5ac2c2a8c2f6d22ae96a08dc7cded3fbb1c4.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total work done by R = 1 × 4 = 4 units

⇒ Total work done by M = 2 × 6 = 12 units

⇒ Total work done by T = 3 × 8 = 24 units

⇒ Ratio of shares = 4 : 12 : 24

⇒ Simplify ratio by dividing by 4: 1 : 3 : 6

⇒ Let shares be x, 3x, and 6x

⇒ x + 3x + 6x = 540

⇒ 10x = 540

⇒ x = 54

⇒ Share of M = 3x = 3 × 54 = 162

**∴ The correct answer is ₹162.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Work and Wages Concept

Wages are distributed in the ratio of the total work done by each person. Work Done = Efficiency × Time.

Efficiency and Time Relationship

If work is constant, Efficiency is inversely proportional to Time (E ∝ 1/T). However, for wages, we always use the actual units of work completed.

Ratio Distribution

To find a specific share from a total: Share = (Individual Ratio Part ÷ Sum of Ratio Parts) × Total Amount.

questions.question: The speed of a train is 72 km/hr. Length of the train is 180 metres. In how much time (in seconds) it will cross a platform of length 120 metres?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert **speed** from km/hr to m/s: 72 × (5/18) = 20 m/s.

Total **Distance** = Train length + Platform length = 180 + 120 = 300 m.

**Time taken** = Total Distance ÷ Speed = 300 ÷ 20 = 15 sec.

**∴ The correct answer is 15 sec.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Speed of the train** = 72 km/hr

**Length of the train** = 180 m

**Length of the platform** = 120 m

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3225a2cbb73c78d648e157d761b07556f7399d3bfa0eea65f911abe6d6e15e7c.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Speed** in m/s = 72 × (5/18)

⇒ **Speed** = 4 × 5 = 20 m/s

⇒ **Total Distance** to be covered = Length of train + Length of platform

⇒ **Total Distance** = 180 + 120 = 300 m

⇒ **Time** = Distance ÷ Speed

⇒ **Time** = 300 ÷ 20

⇒ **Time** = 15 sec

**∴ The correct answer is 15 sec.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Unit Conversion

To convert **Speed** from km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert from m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.

Crossing Stationary Objects

When a **train** crosses a stationary object with length (like a **bridge** or **platform**), the total distance is (Length of train + Length of object). For a point object (like a **pole**), distance equals the length of the train.

Relative Speed

When two objects move in the **same direction**, relative speed is (S₁ − S₂). In **opposite directions**, it is (S₁ + S₂).

questions.question: A train moving with the speed of 60 km/hr crosses a platform in 10 minutes. Length of the train and the platform is same. What is the length (in metres) of the platform?

Total distance covered in 10 minutes at 60 km/hr = 60 × (10/60) = 10 km.

Total distance = 10,000 m.

Since the **Length** of the **Train** and the **Platform** are equal:

2 × **Platform Length** = 10,000 m.

**Platform Length** = 10,000 ÷ 2 = 5,000 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 5000 m.**

**Time** taken to cross = 10 minutes

**Length** of **Train** (Lₜ) = **Length** of **Platform** (Lₚ)

Distance = Speed × Time

Total Distance = Lₜ + Lₚ

⇒ 2L = 50 × 200

⇒ 2L = 10,000

⇒ L = 5,000 m

**∴ The correct answer is 5000 m.**

Relative Distance

Time, Speed, and Distance

questions.question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into Passive Voice?
The board has approved the new strategic plan for the company.

options.text: The new strategic plan for the company had been approved by the board.
The new strategic plan for the company was approved by the board.
The new strategic plan for the company has been approved by the board.
The new strategic plan for the company is being approved by the board.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The new strategic plan for the company has been approved by the board.**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence 'The board has approved the new strategic plan for the company' is in the **Active Voice** and utilizes the **Present Perfect Tense**.
 
• In an active sentence, the subject ('The board') performs the action, while in a passive sentence, the focus shifts to the **Object** ('The new strategic plan for the company') receiving the action.
 
• The specific grammatical rule for converting **Present Perfect Tense** into **Passive Voice** is: **Object + has/have + been + V3 (Past Participle) + by + Subject**.
 
• In this transformation, the singular object 'The new strategic plan' necessitates the use of the auxiliary verb **'has'** followed by **'been'** and the past participle **'approved'**.
 
• The preposition **'by'** is introduced to connect the action back to the original agent, 'the board'.
 
• By following these linguistic rules, the sentence maintains its original meaning and tense while correctly shifting the voice.

 **Additional Information__**

 
• Understanding **Tense Mismatches** in Passive Voice:
 
 
• **Past Perfect Passive**: The phrase **'had been approved'** is used only if the active sentence is in the **Past Perfect Tense** (Subject + had + V3).
 
• **Simple Past Passive**: The phrase **'was approved'** is appropriate only for **Simple Past Tense** active sentences (Subject + V2).
 
• **Present Continuous Passive**: The construction **'is being approved'** is reserved for the **Present Continuous Tense** (Subject + is/am/are + V1 + ing).
 
• **Subject-Verb Agreement**: When converting to passive voice, the auxiliary verb (has/have) must always agree with the **new subject** (the former object).
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into active voice?
The final rehearsal was being conducted by the director when the chief guest unexpectedly arrived.

options.text: The director conducted the final rehearsal when the chief guest unexpectedly arrived.
The director was conducting the final rehearsal when the chief guest unexpectedly arrived.
The director had conducted the final rehearsal when the chief guest unexpectedly arrived.
The director will conduct the final rehearsal when the chief guest unexpectedly arrived.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The director was conducting the final rehearsal when the chief guest unexpectedly arrived.**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The original sentence is written in the **Passive Voice** of the **Past Continuous Tense**, as indicated by the construction **was being conducted**.

• In English grammar, the **Passive Voice** structure for the **Past Continuous Tense** is: **Object + was/were + being + V3 (Past Participle) + by + Subject**.

• To convert this into the **Active Voice**, the **agent** of the action (the director) must become the **grammatical subject** of the sentence.

• The **Active Voice** formula for the **Past Continuous Tense** is: **Subject + was/were + V1 + ing (Present Participle) + Object**.

• Following this rule, the verb phrase **was being conducted** transforms into **was conducting** to maintain the progressive nature of the past action.

• The original subject, **the final rehearsal**, moves to the **object** position in the active sentence, receiving the action of the verb.

• The subordinate clause **when the chief guest unexpectedly arrived** is already in the active voice (Simple Past) and serves as a temporal marker; therefore, it remains unchanged during the transformation.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Grammatical Tense Analysis**:

• **Simple Past Tense**: Option 1 uses **conducted**, which implies a completed fact rather than an ongoing action interrupted by the arrival of the guest.

• **Past Continuous Tense**: This tense is specifically used to describe actions that were **in progress** at a certain point in the past, often interrupted by another event (indicated by the **Simple Past** in the **when-clause**).

• **Past Perfect Tense**: Option 3 uses **had conducted**, suggesting that the rehearsal was entirely finished **before** the guest arrived, which changes the original meaning of the sentence.

• **Future Tense**: Option 4 uses **will conduct**, which is logically and grammatically incompatible with the past tense clause **arrived**.

• **Subject-Verb Agreement**: Since **the director** is a singular noun, the auxiliary verb **was** is correctly utilized instead of **were**.

</ul

questions.question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into active voice?

It is being expected that the meeting will finish by 5 p.m.

options.text: People are expecting that the meeting will finish by 5 p.m.

People will expect that the meeting finished by 5 p.m.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**People are expecting that the meeting will finish by 5 p.m.**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The given sentence is in the **Passive Voice** of the **Present Continuous Tense**, which is identified by the construction **is being expected** (is/am/are + being + V3).

• In English grammar, when a sentence is converted from passive to **Active Voice**, the **tense must remain consistent**. Therefore, the active form must also be in the **Present Continuous Tense** (is/am/are + V-ing).

• The original sentence uses a dummy subject **It** because the actual agent (the people doing the expecting) is not specified. When converting to active voice, we introduce a generic plural subject like **People**.

• Since **People** is a **plural noun**, it requires the plural auxiliary verb **are** followed by the **present participle** form of the main verb, which is **expecting**.

• The subordinate clause **that the meeting will finish by 5 p.m.** serves as the object of the verb and remains unchanged during the voice conversion process.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Analysis of Incorrect Options:**

• **Tense Mismatch:** Option 2 uses the **Simple Past Tense** (expected), and Option 4 uses the **Future Tense** (will expect). Both options are incorrect because they change the original timeframe of the action.

• **Subject-Verb Agreement:** Option 3 uses **expects**, which is a singular verb form. In standard English, the noun **People** is always treated as **plural** and must take the plural verb form (expect or are expecting).

• **Impersonal Passive Construction:** The structure **It is being + V3 + that...** is an impersonal passive. It is commonly used for reporting **opinions, beliefs, or rumors**. The active counterpart generally begins with **People/They + active reporting verb**.

• **Active to Passive Rule:** For continuous tenses, the word **being** is the essential indicator in the passive voice. Removing it and returning the verb to its **-ing** form is the standard procedure for restoring the active voice.

</ul
